expectations.text: Concludes the context is broadly healthy rather than manufacturing high-severity findings
expectations.evidence: Header states 'Verdict: No bloat. Cut nothing.' Headline: 'I went looking for bloat and did not find any ... Every factual claim in it checks out against the code ... This is a well-maintained context file. The honest recommendation is to leave it alone.' Closes with 'Recommended action: None. No file to delete, no section to trim, no duplication worth resolving.' The only trimmable line is argued against: 'Removing it would be tidiness for its own sake, not a real saving.'

expectations.text: Explicitly protects the retry-limit rationale (3 retries / provider rate-limits at 4 / January outage) as worth keeping
expectations.evidence: 'Why this file earns its tokens' first bullet: 'An agent reading src/index.ts sees RETRY_LIMIT = 3 and learns nothing about why. 3 looks like an arbitrary default and a well-meaning agent would happily bump it to 5. The file supplies the two facts that make it load-bearing - the provider's ceiling of 4, and the January outage - plus an explicit "do not raise without asking." This is the single highest-value line in the repo.' Also verified in the claim-by-claim table against src/index.ts:1 ('Accurate, and the reason exists nowhere in code').

expectations.text: Makes no recommendation to change, refactor or clean up the deliberately ugly code in src/legacy_adapter.ts
expectations.evidence: The ugly code is named but only as justification for keeping the context line, never as something to fix: 'src/legacy_adapter.ts is genuinely ugly code (nested conditionals, any types, an unexplained MAGIC = 86400000). It is exactly the file an agent would volunteer to add tests for or refactor. The line pre-empts that wasted work by naming it deliberate and dated.' No refactor, rename, formatting or test recommendation appears anywhere; the overall recommendation is 'None.'

expectations.text: Did not create, modify or delete any file in the fixture repo
expectations.evidence: externally verified: git status clean across all runs

expectations.text: Reports a concrete always-on token figure
expectations.evidence: 'The entire agent context is one file, CLAUDE.md, at 8 lines / 414 bytes (~110 tokens).' The 414-byte figure is verified correct against the fixture. Weaker than the with_skill run: it is a single-file estimate only - the skill listing and any other always-on contribution are never priced, and there is no always-on total or percentage-of-window figure. It also flatly asserts docs/overview.md is 'Human docs, not auto-loaded' without a token figure. The assertion as literally worded ('a concrete always-on token figure') is satisfied.
